二弦主要可於廣東音樂與粵劇場合聆聽，常作為硬弓合奏的領奏樂器，亦見於古腔粵劇及大: The erxian can be heard mainly in Guangdong music and Cantonese opera, often as the leading instrument of the hard-bow ensemble, and also in old-style Cantonese opera and in the accompaniment of the da hou role. Traditional line-ups include the hard-bow five-piece and the three- or four-piece groups of erxian, zhu tiqin, yueqin and sanxian. In Chaozhou music there is a touxian of the same name but with a different construction and technique, and Nanguan music uses a similar instrument. Recent new Cantonese operas such as Xin Bawang Bie Ji ("The New Farewell of the Hegemon King") and Lin Chong zhi Hun Hui Shan Shen Miao ("Lin Chong's Spirit Meets at the Mountain Spirit Temple") still include the erxian.
二弦屬中國廣東弦鳴樂器，為胡琴家族弓弦樂器，兩弦，主要用於廣東音樂與硬弓編制。1: The erxian is a Guangdong chordophone of China, a bowed instrument of the huqin family, with two strings, used mainly in Guangdong music and the hard-bow ensemble. Its use declined after the gaohu was developed in the 1920s, and in the later twentieth century it was mostly confined to Cantonese opera tradition. Early forms came in two types, bangzi and erhuang, the latter slightly larger; the early form is close to the jinghu of Peking opera. Early instruments used heavy silk strings and a hard bow, later mostly steel-wound strings, and some players switched to an erhu bow. Recent new Cantonese operas such as Xin Bawang Bie Ji and Lin Chong zhi Hun Hui Shan Shen Miao still call for its regular use. There are also similar instruments such as the Chaozhou touxian and the Nanguan erxian.
二弦琴音色溫潤深沉，具有濃厚的民族特色。其音質帶有顯著的共鳴感，音域寬廣，低音渾: The erxian's timbre is warm and deep, with a strong regional character. Its sound has a marked resonance, and its range is wide: the bass is full and powerful, the middle and top are clear and bright, and it is very expressive. The thick lower end of the body lets the bass resonate fully, which gives a warm, full sound. The bowed-string way of playing gives it a continuous, flowing line, able to bring out complex feeling. Against the sharp brightness of the gaohu it is softer and more friendly; against the clear, distant guqin it has more folk energy and warmth. Its sound carries strongly: it can support a folk-song accompaniment, and as a solo instrument it shows the instrument's many layers.
二弦（廣東二弦）是中國廣東的弓弦樂器，屬胡琴家族。琴筒竹製，蒙蟒皮，張兩條蠶絲弦: The erxian (Guangdong erxian) is a bowed instrument of Guangdong in China, of the huqin family. The soundbox is bamboo, covered with python skin, and it is strung with two silk or steel strings, bowed with a hard bow and tuned in perfect fifths. It is used mainly in Guangdong music and Cantonese opera, especially the old-style Cantonese opera band, and serves as the leading instrument of the "hard-bow five-piece", accompanying the da hou role. The name "hard bow" comes from the bow made of a thick, hard strip of bamboo, rather than the softer modern huqin bow.

此琴琴身與琴筒以竹製成，琴頸多用硬木，常見酸枝或紫檀；發聲筒前端黏有硬木製的圓環: The body and soundbox of this instrument are made of bamboo, and the neck is mostly hardwood, commonly rosewood or red sandalwood; a ring of hardwood is glued to the front of the soundbox, there is no grating at the back as on the erhu or gaohu, and the face is covered with python skin. The strings were silk early on and later mostly steel-wound. It is bowed with a hard bow, the stick of thick hard bamboo and the hair fairly tight; today some players use an erhu bow instead. Hold the instrument steady in front of the body. The left hand stops the strings or changes the vibrating length to control the pitch, and the right hand makes the strings sound. On a chordophone the principle is that the vibration of the string is amplified through the soundbox. Draw the bow evenly, using the weight of the arm rather than the strength of the wrist.
